name: Schizophrenia
block: Schizophrenia and other primary psychotic disorders (ICD-11)

overview.text: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic illness combining positive symptoms such as delusions and hallucinations with negative symptoms, disorganization and cognitive impairment, typically emerging in late adolescence or early adulthood. Diagnosis remains clinical, anchored in ICD-11 and DSM-5-TR criteria, because no biomarker is validated for routine use.

Most patients achieve substantial recovery of positive symptoms with antipsychotic treatment, while negative and cognitive symptoms respond less and drive long-term disability. Coordinated early-intervention care, relapse prevention and physical-health monitoring determine long-term outcomes as much as drug choice.

description.text: Added experiences such as persecutory delusions, auditory verbal hallucinations, disorganized speech and grossly disorganized behavior. They fluctuate with illness activity and respond best to dopamine-blocking treatment.

Losses of normal function: avolition, asociality, anhedonia, alogia and blunted affect. Primary negative symptoms reflect the illness itself, while secondary ones stem from depression, medication or deprivation and must be distinguished because they are treatable.

Deficits in processing speed, working memory, attention, verbal learning and social cognition are present in most patients and predict functional recovery better than psychotic symptoms do. They respond poorly to antipsychotics and are the main target of cognitive remediation.

Depressive and anxious syndromes are common across all illness stages and carry most of the suicide risk, which concentrates in young men early in the course. Mood symptoms respond to antidepressant augmentation and clozapine, which uniquely reduces suicidality.

Motor signs range from subtle neurological soft signs to full catatonia with stupor, posturing and waxy flexibility, which is a medical emergency. Benzodiazepines and ECT are the definitive catatonia treatments; antipsychotics alone can worsen it.

Impaired awareness of illness is itself a symptom, rooted in frontal dysfunction rather than denial, and it is the strongest predictor of treatment refusal. Psychoeducation, family work and long-acting formulations are built around this fact.

claim.text: The largest coordinated MRI meta-analysis found widespread cortical thinning in schizophrenia, most pronounced in frontal and temporal regions, in chronically ill medicated samples.
Hippocampal volume is reliably reduced, among the largest subcortical effects detected across thousands of scanned individuals.
Whole-amygdala volume reduction is reported at group level; it is shown across all four amygdala sub-meshes here because the source resolves only the whole structure.
Thalamic volume reduction is reported for the whole thalamus; it is distributed across the resolved nuclei groups as a proxy.
Diffusion imaging meta-analysis finds widespread lower fractional anisotropy across commissural, association and projection fibres, indicating distributed white-matter dysconnectivity.
Molecular imaging consistently shows elevated presynaptic dopamine synthesis and release capacity in the striatum, most marked in acute psychosis.

function.text: Excess phasic dopamine here assigns salience to neutral stimuli, which the cortex then explains with delusional narratives; blocking this signal eases positive symptoms.
Blunted cortical dopamine signaling impairs working memory, drive and executive control, mapping onto negative and cognitive symptoms that D2 blockade does not fix.
Weak prefrontal inhibition of an over-reactive amygdala-hippocampal system produces threat bias, paranoia and affective instability.

claim.text: The revised dopamine hypothesis places striatal hyperdopaminergia at the final common pathway of psychosis, with simultaneous prefrontal hypodopaminergia explaining negative and cognitive symptoms.

neurochemistry.alteration: NMDA-receptor hypofunction, especially on parvalbumin interneurons

claim.text: NMDA-receptor blockers reproduce the full symptom spectrum including negative and cognitive features, and risk genes converge on glutamate signalling, supporting upstream glutamate dysfunction. In vivo imaging has since given the glutamate and dopamine pictures greater anatomical and functional specificity than the original pharmacological account.

neurochemistry.alteration: Parvalbumin interneuron deficits with reduced inhibitory tone

claim.text: Post-mortem studies report reduced markers of fast-spiking parvalbumin interneurons, which would disinhibit pyramidal output and desynchronize cortical gamma rhythms.

neurochemistry.alteration: Muscarinic M1/M4 signaling as a non-dopaminergic lever

claim.text: Selective M1/M4 muscarinic agonism treats psychosis without dopamine blockade, as validated by the 2024 approval of xanomeline-trospium.
Cortical 5-HT2A blockade distinguishes second- from first-generation antipsychotics and contributes to their broader tolerability profile.

neurochemistry.alteration: Complement-mediated excessive synaptic pruning during development

claim.text: Structural variation increasing C4A expression raises schizophrenia risk, mechanistically linking immune complement activity to adolescent synaptic pruning.

architecture.text: Risk is highly polygenic: genome-wide association implicates a large number of common loci of individually small effect, enriched in synaptic genes.
On top of polygenic background, rare coding variants and copy-number deletions carry individually large effects, with exome studies converging on glutamatergic and chromatin genes.

A landmark multi-stage genome-wide association study reached genome-wide significance at 108 conservatively defined loci through 128 independent associations, in up to 36,989 cases and 113,075 controls, with 83 of the loci not previously reported.

Associated loci were enriched among genes expressed in brain and, independently of that signal, among genes expressed in tissues important for immunity, which supports immune involvement rather than making it a by-product of brain-expression bias.

Associations at DRD2 and at several genes involved in glutamatergic neurotransmission place genetic risk on the same pathways as the leading dopamine and glutamate hypotheses, so those hypotheses are now partly genetic in origin rather than only pharmacologically derived.

finding.text: Meta-analyses report elevated neutrophil-based inflammatory ratios in psychosis at group level, but heterogeneity is high and no cutoff has diagnostic value.
Circulating IL-6 and related cytokines are elevated on average in psychosis, supporting an inflammatory component without yielding a clinical test.

pathway.step: First episode: antipsychotic monotherapy + coordinated care

claim.text: Guidelines recommend starting one second-generation antipsychotic at the lowest effective dose within coordinated specialty or early-intervention care, with baseline metabolic monitoring.

pathway.step: Partial response: optimize, switch, consider long-acting injectable

claim.text: After an adequate dose and duration without response, guidelines advise switching to a different antipsychotic and considering long-acting injectables where adherence is in doubt.
Resistance is defined by two failed adequate antipsychotic trials; clozapine is then mandatory, with compulsory blood monitoring, not optional.

Catatonia mandates benzodiazepines or ECT; persistent voices may be offered temporoparietal rTMS and negative symptoms prefrontal rTMS or tDCS as adjuncts with modest expected gains, alongside CBT for psychosis and cognitive remediation.
Maintenance focuses on relapse prevention, family involvement, employment support and systematic cardiometabolic monitoring, since cardiovascular disease drives excess mortality.

tour.title: 1 · Risk is written in genes
tour.text: Schizophrenia is among the most heritable psychiatric disorders: hundreds of common variants plus rare large-effect mutations. No single gene causes it.

tour.title: 2 · Dopamine runs hot in the striatum
tour.text: Molecular imaging shows excess presynaptic dopamine in the caudate, putamen and accumbens — the final common pathway of psychosis.

tour.title: 3 · The salience circuit misfires
tour.text: Excess striatal dopamine makes neutral events feel significant; the cortex invents delusions to explain them. Watch the mesolimbic loop.

tour.title: 4 · Cortex thins and disconnects
tour.text: Frontal and temporal cortex thin out while white-matter integrity falls across commissural and association fibres.

tour.title: 5 · Symptoms map to systems
tour.text: Voices track auditory-language cortex, paranoia tracks threat circuits, apathy tracks prefrontal drive. Pick a domain to light its circuit.

tour.title: 6 · Drugs work at receptors
tour.text: Every antipsychotic touches D2; the newer ones add serotonin, muscarinic or partial-agonist actions. Adverse effects map to the same receptors.

tour.title: 7 · The guideline pathway
tour.text: One antipsychotic plus coordinated care first; switch on failure; clozapine for resistance; targeted adjuncts for what remains.

quiz.question: What are the ICD-11 and DSM-5-TR codes for schizophrenia?
quiz.explanation: ICD-11 lists schizophrenia under 6A20 and DSM-5-TR under 295.90; the other pairs belong to depression, bipolar disorder and OCD.

quiz.question: Which of these is a negative symptom rather than a positive symptom?
quiz.explanation: Avolition (loss of drive) is a core negative symptom; the rest are positive symptoms reflecting added experiences.

quiz.question: A patient improves on antidepressants and sleep, and the 'negative symptoms' resolve. What were they most likely?
quiz.explanation: Secondary negative symptoms stem from depression, medication or deprivation and remit when the cause is treated; primary ones reflect the illness itself.

quiz.question: According to the revised dopamine hypothesis, which pattern holds in schizophrenia?
choices: Normal dopamine with pure glutamate excess
quiz.explanation: Version III of the hypothesis pairs mesolimbic hyperdopaminergia (psychosis) with mesocortical hypodopaminergia (negative/cognitive symptoms).

quiz.question: The ENIGMA cortical meta-analysis found which pattern in schizophrenia?
quiz.explanation: Across 4474 patients, thinning was widespread with the largest effects in frontal and temporal cortex.

quiz.question: Which subcortical finding is most replicated in ENIGMA schizophrenia data?
quiz.explanation: Hippocampal (plus amygdala and thalamic) volume reductions are among the most replicated subcortical findings.

quiz.question: What did the ENIGMA-DTI study report in schizophrenia?
quiz.explanation: Across 4322 individuals, white-matter integrity was lower across commissural, association and projection fibres.

quiz.question: What does the C4A finding imply about schizophrenia biology?
quiz.explanation: C4A structural variation increasing expression implicates overactive complement-mediated pruning during development.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes schizophrenia genetic architecture?
choices: Polygenic common variants plus rare large-effect variants
quiz.explanation: Hundreds of common loci of small effect combine with rare coding variants and CNVs such as 22q11.2 of large effect.

quiz.question: What striatal D2 occupancy pattern is associated with response versus motor side effects?
choices: Response at substantial blockade, EPS/prolactin as blockade climbs higher
Higher occupancy always means better response
quiz.explanation: Response tracks substantial D2 blockade while pushing occupancy higher buys mainly extrapyramidal symptoms and prolactin rise.

quiz.question: When is clozapine indicated?
choices: After two failed adequate antipsychotic trials
As routine first-line for every patient
quiz.explanation: TRRIP criteria define resistance as two failed adequate trials, at which point clozapine with blood monitoring is mandatory, not optional.

quiz.question: What is distinctive about xanomeline-trospium (Cobenfy)?
choices: Treats psychosis via muscarinic agonism without D2 blockade
It is a D2 partial agonist
quiz.explanation: FDA-approved in September 2024, it stimulates central M1/M4 receptors while trospium blocks peripheral muscarinic effects — the first non-dopaminergic mechanism.

quiz.question: Ulotaront (TAAR1 agonist) development status is best described as:
quiz.explanation: Both DIAMOND 1 and 2 missed their primary endpoints, a reminder that novel mechanisms must survive late-stage trials.

quiz.question: Which neuromodulation is definitive for catatonia in psychosis?
quiz.explanation: Guidelines position benzodiazepines and ECT as the definitive catatonia treatments; antipsychotics alone may worsen it.

quiz.question: Which psychosocial interventions do guidelines recommend for all patients with psychosis?
choices: CBT for psychosis and family interventions
quiz.explanation: NICE recommends offering CBTp and family interventions alongside medication, plus coordinated early-intervention care.

quiz.question: What is the current status of inflammatory blood ratios (NLR/PLR) in schizophrenia?
choices: Group-level elevation with no diagnostic cutoff
quiz.explanation: Meta-analyses show average elevations in psychosis, but heterogeneity is high and nothing has diagnostic validity — an emerging signal, not a test.
